title: Interrupts and the Interrupt Service Routine
intro: Catch up on the key A Level ideas. Complete four retrieval questions, work through the examples, then practise and explain your reasoning.

questions.prompt: With page size 1,024 bytes, what offset is address 2,500?
For the binary value 1010, what is its decimal value?
A linked-list node has data and what other essential field?
questions.answer: A link/reference to the next node (for a singly linked list).

questions.answer: In its left subtree (under the chosen no-duplicate convention).

blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: ISR — Routine that services a particular interrupt.
context — CPU state needed to resume execution.
polling — Repeated checking of a device or condition.

blocks.title: Event occurs
blocks.text: A device or timer signals that attention is needed.

blocks.title: State is preserved
blocks.text: The CPU completes a suitable instruction boundary and saves essential context.

blocks.title: Service and return
blocks.text: The ISR handles the event; saved context is restored and execution resumes.

blocks.title: Worked example · Model answer
blocks.text: After completing the current instruction and recognising the interrupt, the CPU preserves relevant state, runs the keyboard ISR to obtain the key event, restores state and resumes the interrupted program. Check: link each claim to the scenario and use precise OCR terminology.

blocks.title: Shared worked answer
blocks.text: The disk raises an interrupt; the CPU saves context when accepted; the ISR acknowledges completion and updates status; the original process resumes or the scheduler selects another ready process.
